advices.diagnosis: The class exhibits low cohesion (LCOM4=2) and high coupling to infrastructure (DCC=2), violating the presentation layer's architectural constraints by directly importing `OrderRepository` and `EmailClient`. The `describe_customer` method displays feature envy towards the `customer` object, accessing its attributes four times while only using one local attribute. The class acts as a thin wrapper over infrastructure components, which is inappropriate for a presentation layer that should depend on application or domain abstractions.

suggestions.title: Introduce application layer services to decouple from infrastructure
suggestions.sketch: Replace `OrderRepository` and `EmailClient` dependencies with application layer interfaces (e.g., `OrderQueryService` and `NotificationService`). The `ReportView` should accept these services in its constructor. This moves the infrastructure dependency out of the presentation layer, resolving the LV-SKIP violations. The `order_count` and `mail_summary` methods will delegate to these services, reducing direct coupling to infra classes.

suggestions.title: Extract customer formatting logic to a domain or application service
suggestions.sketch: Move the `describe_customer` logic to a `CustomerFormatter` in the domain or application layer. The `ReportView` will call `formatter.format(customer)` instead of accessing `customer` attributes directly. This reduces feature envy and improves cohesion by separating formatting concerns from the view class. The `ReportView` will no longer need to know the structure of `Customer`.

advices.risk_notes: Introducing new application layer services requires defining their interfaces and implementations, which may increase the number of classes in the project. However, this is a necessary step to respect layer boundaries. The feature envy extraction is low-risk as it is a pure refactoring of string formatting logic. Ensure that the new services are properly tested and that the `ReportView` remains a thin presentation component.
